finding: Current Branch vehicle lineage closes reliability/serviceability/recovery effects for Type 95/97 families but intentionally does not yet propagate those causes through successor-tank development, production conversion, and field allocation. This is an unresolved downstream layer, not evidence that later tanks stay historical by rule.

historical_baseline.Type97_Kai: 47mm Shinhoto line is already a historical 1942-43 production family and must be unit/date gated, not treated as a rare future technology.
historical_baseline.Type1_ChiHe: Design accepted early-war; historical production begins 1943, total roughly 170 through 1944. Improvements include 47mm gun, five-man crew/three-man turret logic, more powerful engine, welded/thicker hull and standard radio.
historical_baseline.Type3_ChiNu: Historical urgent development starts May 1943 and design is completed around October 1943; regular production historically waits until late 1944, with steel/resource priority an important bottleneck.
historical_baseline.Type4_ChiTo: Separate heavier/new-generation line. Prototype-stage during 1944; not a credible mass battlefield asset in 1944H1 without a much larger industrial divergence.

branch_causal_effects_to_audit: compute/metrology -> stress, recoil, turret-balance and tolerance calculations close faster
production statistics/QC -> fewer prototype and early-series rejection loops
welding/process control -> Chi-He-class hull production is easier to stabilize
engine/reliability line -> 240hp-class powertrain acceptance and field reliability improve, but engine count remains an industrial gate
optics/bore/ammunition-lot repeatability -> better first-round and repeat-fire consistency without changing penetration
radio/communications maturity -> standard radio and five-man crew yield more operational value than historical Japanese flag-command practice
Nomonhan and 1942-43 combat feedback -> anti-armor requirement remains real even if Type97 reliability is better
Sherman intelligence/combat reports -> pushes 75mm stopgap priority, but does not create steel or factories
Navy/aircraft/ship steel priority -> remains the dominant cap on mass production unless separately changed

Type97_Kai.rule: retain historical-family availability and likely broad 1942-43 fielding; Branch benefit is readiness/QC, not automatic extra hulls
Type97_Kai.warning: future OOBs must distinguish 57mm Type97 from 47mm Kai instead of generic 'Type97' when antitank combat matters

Type1_ChiHe.1944_02_status: production line definitely exists; cumulative physical count needs a factory ledger before locking
Type1_ChiHe.branch_timing_effect: 0-3 months earlier stable production/tooling is plausible; large quantity multiplication is not
Type1_ChiHe.allocation: home/training/selected armored formations first unless a dated shipping/theater decision sends them overseas

Type3_ChiNu.1944_02_status: design/tooling or pilot/pre-series stage; no regular combat unit assumed yet
Type3_ChiNu.branch_timing_effect: design freeze may move ~1-2 months earlier and low-rate production gate ~2-4 months earlier than historical if steel is allocated
Type3_ChiNu.working_regular_production_gate: 1944-04..06 rather than automatic historical late-1944; must pass steel/factory/priority gate
Type3_ChiNu.combat_effect: potentially relevant to Home Islands/late-1944 deployments; Marianas availability requires both production and physically credible shipping before the battle

Type4_ChiTo.rule: computation can reduce iteration, but new hull, gun, engine and mass/steel requirements remain; no 1944H1 combat unit

doctrine_and_support_propagation: A more reliable Chi-Ha does not remove the need for 47mm antitank firepower; it may make armored formations more credible organizationally.
Three-man turret/standard-radio value should be evaluated separately from armor/gun penetration.
Recovery tractors, workshops, spare packs and tank transport matter to successor units too.
Type 1 47mm towed AT guns and Ho-Ni/other SPG lines should be audited alongside tanks because Japan may rationally solve Sherman locally with gun vehicles rather than only new medium tanks.
Do not infer 'better tank doctrine' universally; require unit training and combined-arms evidence.
required_before_next_tank_sensitive_camp: 1943-44 monthly Japanese tank/AFV factory output by family
unit conversion and depot acceptance dates
57mm Type97 vs 47mm Kai composition by tank regiment
Chi-He/Chi-Nu/SPG/AT-gun availability as one common antitank wallet

immediate_effect_on_existing_settlements.Tarawa: no change without evidence that its 14 Type95 vehicles were a different family
immediate_effect_on_existing_settlements.Bengal: no change; independent tank regiment remains absent
immediate_effect_on_existing_settlements.Saipan_future_working: must be re-opened before promotion because 'Type97/Type95' generic composition may understate 47mm Kai share and because an early Chi-He/Chi-Nu shipping decision has not been audited
immediate_effect_on_existing_settlements.China_1944_future: Tank Regiment No.3 physical count can stand provisionally, but model mix and 47mm/Chi-He share need the same production ledger
